According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple is preparing significant changes to its physical retail stores ahead of the launch of its Home product line. Apple is expected to unveil updated versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K as early as this autumn, with related changes seemingly hinting that a third, more important product will debut simultaneously.

Apple has accumulated a large backlog of unreleased Home products, largely due to repeated delays in the Siri revamp. Now that the Siri overhaul is finally complete, we can expect some of these products to finally hit the market after years without updates.

However, earlier reports had suggested that Apple would first launch updated versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K, with the company's first smart home hub (namely a HomePod or HomePad with built-in display) potentially arriving later.

Nonetheless, based on current preparations at retail stores, this smart home hub may launch alongside the updated Apple TV and HomePod mini, according to the Power On newsletter:

Of course, the final answer will have to wait for Apple's September event. But based on today's report, Apple's all-new smart home hub stands a good chance of debuting alongside the updated Apple TV 4K, as well as a HomePod mini supporting Siri AI.

Key Highlights

In summary, Apple's smart home hub is widely rumoured to feature a 7-inch square display, with two versions planned: one with a built-in speaker, and another with magnets on the back for wall mounting. The product will run an all-new operating system with a home screen that supports widgets. Besides serving as a FaceTime video calling device, it will of course act as the central hub for all smart home accessories and Siri. The device will also include an A18 chip.

Another rumour about the Home product line is that the next-generation Apple TV 4K may come with an updated Siri Remote, though the specific changes remain unclear for now.

Are you interested in the new Home products? Which one are you most looking forward to? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
